--- # title: "The BIDE model" # subtitle: "Applied Population Dynamics WILD 5700/7700" format: revealjs: theme: default pagetitle: "The BIDE model" slide-number: true toc: false # toc-title: "Today's topics" # center: false margin: 0.1 lang: en --- # Definitions {visibility="hidden"} ## {content-align="center" style="font-size: 110%;"}
**The BIDE Model** ::: {style="font-size: 90%;"} Applied Population Dynamics WILD 5700/7700 :::
![](lecture-BIDE_files/figure-html/bide0-1.png){width="60%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="BIDE model"} ## Today's class
::: {style="font-size: 1.2em;"} 1. A few definitions 2. Modeling 101 3. The BIDE model ::: ## Definitions ::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"} **Population dynamics**: The study of spatial and temporal variation in population *size* and *structure*
::: {.fragment} **Population**: Individuals of the same species occuring in the same geographic region :::
::: {.fragment} **Population size and structure** - *Size*: Abundance - *Structure*: Distribution of individuals among age groups, sexes, habitat patches, etc... ::: ::: # Modeling 101 {visibility="hidden"} ## Models and science A model is an abstraction of reality that describes the relationship between two or more variables. ::: {.fragment} Models help us... ::: nonincremental - Describe complex natural systems in
a manageable way - Formalize and evaluate hypotheses - Predict future outcomes - ...all while accounting for uncertainty ::: ![](figs/issj.png){.absolute top="200" right="100" height="250" fig-alt="Island Scrub Jay"} ![](figs/jay-model.png){.absolute top="480" right="-50" height="150" fig-alt="Island Scrub Jay density"} ::: ## Models and science *But don't models require assumptions?* . . . Yes. We have to simplify, so we have to make assumptions. We do this all the time. ::: {.notes} , for example when deciding how long it will take you to get to class. :::
. . . ![image](figs/box.jpg){width="30%"} "All models are wrong, but some are useful." G.E.P. Box (1987) ## Model validation
Putting the model to the test ::: columns ::: {.column width="45%"} - How well does it predict? - Will your results hold up in court? - Can your results be replicated/reproduced? ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ![](figs/nasa-prediction.png){width="100%" fig-align="center" fig-alt="NASA climate models"} ::: ::: ## Types of models - Conceptual - Physical - Graphical - Mathematical - Statistical ![](figs/atm-model.png){.absolute top="10" right="70" width="400"} ![](figs/hrrr-model.jpg){.absolute top="410" right="350" width="390"} # BIDE {visibility="hidden"} ## The BIDE model $$N_{t+1} = N_t + B_t + I_t - D_t - E_t$$ $N_t$: population size (state variable) at time $t$\ $B_t$: births\ $I_t$: immigrants\ $D_t$: deaths\ $E_t$: emigrants ## The BIDE model ![](lecture-BIDE_files/figure-revealjs/bide0-1.png){width="75%" fig-align="center"} ## The BIDE model $$N_{t+1} = N_t + B_t + I_t - D_t - E_t$$ As written, this model implies the following: ::: incremental - $B$, $I$, $D$, and $E$ are not rates, they are the number of events at time $t$. - The model is **deterministic**, not **stochastic** - Time is discrete, not continuous ::: . . . In reality, things are more complicated, and interest lies in understanding the factors influencing each process. ## Group exercise
::: {.text-center} Split into groups of 4--6 students.
Come up with a list of at least 5 factors that influence the four demographic variables: B, I, D, and E.
Be prepared to explain which demographic variables are influenced by each factor. ::: # Assignment {visibility="hidden"} ## Assignment
Read the first 3 pages of Chapter 3 in Conroy and Carroll.
Expect a quiz next time we meet.

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
